questions.prompt: Explain the difference between the editor's draft and the accepted board, and why stable ids matter for round progress.

keyPoints.text: A draft is only a proposal; the saved board is what has been accepted.
keyPoints.quote: A draft is a proposal. The saved board is the accepted state.

keyPoints.text: Changing the screen before persistence succeeds loses the update on reload.
keyPoints.quote: the screen changes before persistence succeeds, then a reload loses the apparent update

keyPoints.text: On a storage error the proposal stays in the dialog and the board is untouched.
keyPoints.quote: A storage error leaves the proposal visible in the dialog and the accepted board unchanged.

keyPoints.text: Ids identify records independently of their position.
keyPoints.quote: Stable ids distinguish records from positions.

keyPoints.text: Round progress stores question ids, not indices.
keyPoints.quote: round progress stores question ids

keyPoints.text: Category and question ids share one uniqueness set.
keyPoints.quote: because both go through one `claim()` set

questions.prompt: Why is a Web Lock not enough to prevent lost updates between tabs, and how do the raw-string baseline and derived revision close the gap?

keyPoints.text: The lock only serializes saves that cooperate on the same origin.
keyPoints.quote: A Web Lock serializes cooperating saves on the same origin.

keyPoints.text: A tab that acquires the lock later may still hold an outdated draft.
keyPoints.quote: its draft was still based on revision zero

keyPoints.text: Save compares stored text with the text remembered when the draft began.
keyPoints.quote: compares the current stored text with the exact text remembered when that draft began

keyPoints.text: The comparison uses the raw string rather than the revision number.
keyPoints.quote: The comparison is on the **raw string**, not the parsed object or the revision number.

keyPoints.text: The next revision is computed from storage, not taken from the candidate.
keyPoints.quote: The next revision is computed from current storage

keyPoints.text: This is coarse, whole-board concurrency.
keyPoints.quote: two tabs editing different questions still conflict

keyPoints.text: The guarantee only holds if every writer uses the lock protocol.
keyPoints.quote: The storage guarantee assumes every writer uses the same lock protocol.

questions.prompt: Walk through how missing, empty and corrupt stored data are handled, and why validation and safe rendering are separate defences.

keyPoints.text: Missing data shows examples and writes nothing until the first save.
keyPoints.quote: nothing is written until the first save

keyPoints.text: An empty category list is a valid board.
keyPoints.quote: valid; the board says so

keyPoints.text: Corrupt data disables tiles and editing while keeping the raw text.
keyPoints.quote: shows the examples with tiles and editing disabled

keyPoints.text: Even explicit replacement still runs the baseline comparison first.
keyPoints.quote: so an old recovery screen cannot overwrite a newer repair from another tab

keyPoints.text: Angle brackets in a name can be legitimate text and are not stripped.
keyPoints.quote: A category name containing angle brackets can be valid literal text

keyPoints.text: The renderer uses textContent so values never become elements.
keyPoints.quote: so the value does not create elements

keyPoints.text: None of these defences establish who owns the data.
keyPoints.quote: None of these create authenticated ownership.
